title: daisugi
text: showcasing use daisugi classification. dataset comes forested, tabular data repo lists forest attributes & whether area “forested” “non-forested”.
code: library(daisugi) library(forested) library(rsample)  # defining splits for training and testing datasets splits <- rsample::initial_split(forested::forested) training <- rsample::training(splits) testing <- rsample::testing(splits)   # (x, y) Training: x_train <- training |>   # target (and factors as not all engines handle cats)   dplyr::select(-forested, -tree_no_tree, -land_type, -county)  # our target variable: y_train <- training |> dplyr::select(forested) |> dplyr::pull()  # (x, y) Testing: x_test <- testing |>   dplyr::select(-forested, -tree_no_tree, -land_type, -county)  y_test <- testing |> dplyr::select(forested) |> dplyr::pull()  head(y_test) #> [1] Yes Yes Yes Yes No  No  #> Levels: Yes No

title: daisugi
text: YDF provides various methods boosters, decisions, forests. unique oblique random split technique. daisugi provides boosted method yggdrasil.
code: ydf_trees <- grow_yggdrasil_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 20L ) #> Downloading uv...Done! #> Train model on 5330 examples #> Model trained in 0:00:00.138209  harvest_yggdrasil_trees(ydf_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "No"  "No"

title: daisugi
text: SnapML IBM ML repository. within , contains various ML engines, including implementation called SnapBoost. SnapBoost differs XGBoost using Heterogeneous Newton Boosting. addition, iteration, SnapBoost method randomly chooses whether use decision tree variable depth linear regressor random fourier features.
code: snap_trees <- grow_snap_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 10L )  harvest_snap_trees(snap_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "No" "No" "No" "No" "No" "No"

title: daisugi
text: Perpetual budget-based boosting methodology. perpetual designed drop-automl-like booster require hyperparameter optimization. idea , user can increase budget, ‘predictive power’ parameter, loss plateaus.
code: perpetual_trees <- grow_perpetual_trees(   x_train,   y_train )  harvest_perpetual_trees(perpetual_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] 0 0 0 0 1 1

title: daisugi
text: WildWood new (2021) & advanced random forest algorithm. … “predictions produced WildWood aggregation exponential weights (computed --bag samples) predictions given possible prunings tree.” differs standard random forest.
code: wild_trees <- grow_wild_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 10L )  harvest_wild_trees(wild_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "No"  "No"

title: daisugi
text: “Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) tree-based, cyclic gradient boosting Generalized Additive Model automatic interaction detection.” EBMs considered ‘glassbox’ easier interpret, effective traditional GAMS, “…often accurate SOTA blackbox models” maintaining interpetability.
code: explainable_trees <- grow_explainable_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 100L )  harvest_explainable_trees(wild_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "No"  "No"
